best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
As we look back at Broadway shows that opened in 2020—a year that would prove transformative for the theater industry—several productions stand out for their artistic ambition and critical reception. Despite the unprecedented challenges that would soon shutter theaters worldwide, the shows that premiered before the shutdown demonstrated remarkable range, from bold reimaginings of classics to intimate character studies.

Leading the pack is a revitalized *Les Misérables*, which earns the highest marks from critics for its slicker staging in a newly refurbished venue. The production proves that even well-worn material can feel fresh with the right creative vision. Close behind is *A Soldier's Play*, Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama making its long-awaited Broadway debut. Critics consistently praise the production's powerful performances and the play's enduring relevance, even as some note its conventional staging approach.

The top-rated shows from this period reflect Broadway's ongoing tension between reverence and reinvention. Ivo van Hove's radical *West Side Story* sharply divides critics with its departure from Jerome Robbins' iconic choreography and incorporation of video projections, while more traditional offerings like Bess Wohl's *Grand Horizons* earn praise for stellar ensemble work in a Neil Simon-esque comedy. Meanwhile, *My Name is Lucy Barton* showcases how a luminous star performance—in this case, Laura Linney's—can elevate material that otherwise leaves critics split on its theatrical merits.

With an average critic score of 75 out of 100, the shows that opened in 2020 represent a solid snapshot of Broadway's diversity before an unprecedented pause. Whether you're drawn to ambitious reinterpretations or more conventional storytelling, these productions offer insight into where American theater stood at a pivotal moment.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
As of April 2026, Broadway continues to showcase an impressive collection of productions that first opened in 2021, a pivotal year that marked the industry's triumphant return following the pandemic shutdown. These shows now represent some of the most critically acclaimed work on Broadway, with an average critic score of 82 out of 100.

Leading the rankings is Rebecca Frecknall's immersive revival of Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club, which transforms the August Wilson Theatre into a complete Weimar-era nightclub experience. Critics consistently praise this production's bold environmental staging and its ability to make a classic musical feel urgently contemporary. Close behind is Dana H., an experimental work that pushes theatrical boundaries through Deirdre O'Connell's extraordinary performance, which critics describe as mesmerizing and utterly unique in its approach to storytelling.

The 2021 class also includes Sam Mendes' epic staging of The Lehman Trilogy, which traces 163 years of American capitalism through three virtuosic performances, and Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped revival of Company, which brought fresh perspective to Stephen Sondheim's masterwork. The year proved significant for new voices as well, with Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's Pass Over making history as the first show to open following Broadway's shutdown.

From intimate experimental pieces like Is This a Room to spectacular long-runners like The Phantom of the Opera, the top-rated productions from 2021 demonstrate remarkable range in style, scale, and subject matter. Whether you're drawn to immersive theatrical experiences, innovative storytelling techniques, or reimagined classics, these critically acclaimed shows offer compelling reasons to experience Broadway's artistry firsthand.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
As we reach April 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2022 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. That season proved to be a watershed moment for theatrical innovation and artistic excellence, with productions earning an impressive average critic score of 84 out of 100.

Leading the pack is ABBA Voyage, a technological marvel that pushes the boundaries of live performance with its groundbreaking holographic "ABBAtars." Critics consistently praise the production for creating an experience so convincing it blurs the line between reality and digital artistry. Close behind, Kimberly Akimbo stands out as an intimate musical achievement, with reviewers celebrating its rare ability to balance sharp humor with genuine emotional depth. The show's refreshing originality has made it one of the season's most beloved productions.

The 2022 season also marked a significant moment for revivals, with Into the Woods offering a pared-down Encores! production that serves as a transcendent tribute to Stephen Sondheim. Meanwhile, Pulitzer Prize-winning works dominated the landscape, from Michael R. Jackson's brazenly original A Strange Loop to Suzan-Lori Parks' electrifying Topdog/Underdog revival and Stephen Guirgis's Between Riverside and Crazy.

The diversity of voices and theatrical forms from this season remains striking, encompassing everything from Mike Birbiglia's masterful solo storytelling to Ntozake Shange's groundbreaking choreopoem for colored girls and Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire Ain't No Mo'. Whether you're drawn to technological spectacle, intimate character studies, or bold social commentary, the top-rated shows from 2022 offer something for every theater lover seeking exceptional Broadway experiences.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
As April 2026 unfolds, Broadway continues to showcase an exceptional collection of productions that first opened their doors in 2023, with critics maintaining an impressive average score of 83 out of 100 across the top-rated shows. This remarkable consistency speaks to a vintage year that brought both artistic innovation and commercial success to the Theater District.

Leading the critical pack is "Operation Mincemeat," the British musical phenomenon that journeyed from fringe theater to West End triumph before conquering Broadway. The five-person ensemble piece earns widespread acclaim for its inventive storytelling and infectious energy, proving that intimate productions can deliver outsized impact. Close behind, "Buena Vista Social Club" captures hearts with its exuberant celebration of Cuban music, while Daniel Radcliffe's "Merrily We Roll Along" accomplishes the near-impossible: transforming Stephen Sondheim's legendary 1981 misfire into a critically beloved hit that resonates with contemporary audiences.

The diversity of highly-rated productions reflects Broadway's expanding creative palette. Alex Edelman's solo show "Just for Us" demonstrates that one performer and a compelling true story can command a stage as effectively as elaborate spectacles like "Stranger Things: The First Shadow," which dazzles with jaw-dropping technical effects. Meanwhile, classic revivals including "Sweeney Todd" and "Purlie Victorious" prove that both beloved favorites and overlooked gems deserve renewed attention, while contemporary works like "Appropriate" and "Prima Facie" tackle urgent social themes through powerful dramatic performances.

Whether you're drawn to intimate storytelling, lavish musical productions, or thought-provoking drama, these critically acclaimed shows from 2023's Broadway season offer something for every theatergoer. Explore the full rankings to find your next unforgettable theatrical experience.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
As we move through April 2026, Broadway continues to showcase an exceptional lineup of productions that first opened their doors in 2024. This collection of shows demonstrates remarkable range, from intimate character studies to spectacular musical reimaginings, with an impressive average critic score of 83 out of 100.

Leading the pack is David Adjmi's *Stereophonic*, a meticulously crafted drama set in the 1970s rock scene that critics have embraced as a theatrical marvel. Its authentic depiction of the creative process has resonated deeply with reviewers, earning it the highest critical acclaim among current productions. Close behind, Matthew Bourne's revival of *Oliver!* brings fresh vitality to Lionel Bart's beloved musical, with critics praising its stylish staging and inventive choreography.

The season also features notable diversity in storytelling approaches. *Maybe Happy Ending*, a Korean import exploring romance between obsolete robots, has been hailed as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years. Meanwhile, Cole Escola's *Oh, Mary!* offers irreverent comedy through its outrageous reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln, proving that bold creative risks can pay off with both critics and audiences.

Dance-driven narratives have also found their place, with Justin Peck's *Illinoise* transforming Sufjan Stevens' album into an emotionally moving theatrical experience. Traditional revivals like *Gypsy*, featuring Audra McDonald's powerhouse performance, demonstrate that classic material still resonates when executed with skill and emotional depth.

Whether you're drawn to innovative new works, reimagined classics, or intimate dramas, the highest-rated shows from 2024 offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
Broadway's 2025 season continues to resonate strongly with critics in April 2026, delivering an impressive average score of 86 out of 100 across the year's top-rated productions. The season showcases remarkable range, from intimate dramas exploring identity and memory to spectacular family musicals that push the boundaries of theatrical craft.

**Paddington The Musical** leads the critical pack with its universally praised puppet design and heartfelt storytelling about kindness and acceptance. The production demonstrates how family entertainment can achieve both technical excellence and emotional depth, earning the highest marks among all shows that opened last year. Close behind, the West End transfer of **The Producers** reminds audiences why Mel Brooks's comedy remains a masterclass in musical theater satire, while Ivo van Hove's **All My Sons** proves that classic American drama still has urgent things to say when placed in the hands of visionary directors and powerhouse casts led by Bryan Cranston.

The season's strength extends beyond its frontrunners. **Liberation** brings 1970s feminist history into sharp contemporary focus, while the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** demonstrates the enduring appeal of well-crafted musical comedy. Sondheim's **Into the Woods** receives fresh interpretation, and **Ragtime** returns with timely resonance and vocal performances that critics describe as transcendent.

What unites these top-rated productions is their commitment to theatrical craft—whether through innovative stagecraft in **My Neighbour Totoro**, bold musical storytelling in **Dead Outlaw**, or the linguistic intimacy of Pulitzer winner **English**. For theatergoers planning their Broadway calendar, these critically acclaimed shows represent the best of what last year's season has to offer.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
Broadway's spring 2026 season showcases an intriguing mix of intimate storytelling and bold biographical drama, with solo performances and literary adaptations dominating the critical conversation this April.

Leading the pack is "Every Brilliant Thing," where Daniel Radcliffe delivers what critics describe as a disarmingly warm performance in this interactive one-person play exploring suicide prevention and life's small pleasures. The production's direct audience engagement and emotional accessibility have resonated strongly with reviewers, earning it the highest marks among new openings this season.

Close behind is "Giant," Mark Rosenblatt's provocative drama featuring John Lithgow in a tour-de-force portrayal of Roald Dahl. Critics highlight Lithgow's fearless commitment to depicting the beloved children's author's darker complexities, making this biographical work one of the season's most talked-about productions. The play's unflinching examination of Dahl's controversial legacy has sparked considerable discussion among theatergoers and reviewers alike.

The season also includes "Dog Day Afternoon," a stage adaptation of the iconic 1975 film, though critics note the production struggles to find consistent footing between comedy and drama. This mixed reception reflects a broader trend this spring, where ambitious adaptations face the challenge of translating cinematic classics to the stage.

Overall, April 2026's Broadway landscape leans toward character-driven narratives and performance showcases rather than spectacle, with an average critical score of 70 out of 100 suggesting solid if not universally exceptional work. Whether you're drawn to interactive theatrical experiences, biographical deep dives, or curious about how classic films translate to live performance, the current Broadway season offers multiple entry points for different theatrical tastes.
